project.name: cargo-tracker
project.description: Eclipse Cargo Tracker: a Jakarta EE sample application demonstrating Domain-Driven Design for end-to-end shipping cargo tracking. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Eclipse Cargo Tracker is a Jakarta EE sample application showing Domain-Driven Design for end-to-end cargo shipping: booking, routing, handling and tracking. Start with the README for goals and setup.

tour.title: Build and Runtime Configuration
tour.description: There is no single main(); this is a WAR deployed to a Jakarta EE server. pom.xml defines the build, web.xml configures the web container, and persistence.xml/beans.xml configure JPA and CDI.

tour.title: The Cargo Aggregate
tour.description: The domain layer is the heart of the app. Cargo is the central aggregate, identified by TrackingId, with a RouteSpecification and Itinerary describing where it must go and how.

tour.title: Locations and Voyages
tour.description: Cargo moves between Locations (UnLocode) on Voyages (VoyageNumber, scheduled carrier movements). These value objects and entities are the most widely referenced types in the codebase.

tour.title: Handling Events
tour.description: HandlingEvent records real-world things happening to cargo (load, unload, claim). Events are created via a factory and aggregated into a HandlingHistory, which drives cargo delivery status.

tour.title: Repositories and Domain Services
tour.description: The domain declares repository interfaces and a RoutingService interface; implementations live in the infrastructure layer, keeping the domain free of technical concerns.

tour.title: Application Services
tour.description: Application services orchestrate use cases without holding business rules: booking and routing cargo, registering handling events, and inspecting cargo, with ApplicationEvents as a messaging abstraction.

tour.title: Infrastructure: Persistence, Messaging, Routing
tour.description: Infrastructure implements the domain contracts: JPA repositories for storage, JMS for asynchronous handling-event registration, and ExternalRoutingService calling the pathfinder.

tour.title: Pathfinder Service
tour.description: A small separate REST module computes candidate transit paths over a graph of locations; ExternalRoutingService consumes it.

tour.title: Interfaces: Facade and DTOs
tour.description: The booking facade shields the UI from the domain by exposing DTOs, built by assemblers.

tour.title: Inbound Handling: REST and Real-time
tour.description: External systems report handling events via REST; the app also pushes live tracking updates to clients over WebSockets.

tour.title: Web UI: JSF Pages
tour.description: The UI uses JSF/Facelets: CDI backing beans plus XHTML pages and templates for booking, the admin dashboard and public tracking.

tour.title: Sample Data and Tests
tour.description: SampleDataGenerator seeds locations, voyages and cargo for demos; tests cover the domain and application services.
